sentences.text: United India Insurance Company Ltd., vs Sri B.Ananda Rao And
2 Others

on 15 December, 2023
 The Honourable Smt. Justice M.G.Priyadarsini
 Civil Miscellaneous Appeal No.622 of 2012
Judgment:

1. The present Civil Miscellaneous Appeal has been directed against order dated 16.12.2010 in W.C.No.164 of 2009 on the file of the Commissioner for Workmen's Compensation and Assistant Commissioner of Labour-II, Hyderabad (hereinafter referred to as 'Commissioner').

The said case was filed by respondent Nos.1 and 2 herein seeking compensation for death of one Sri B.
Seetharama Raju @ Seethaiah, who died in an accident that occurred on 26.10.2009 and the same was partly allowed by the Commissioner granting compensation of Rs.4,14,215/-.

Aggrieved by the same, the present Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is filed at the instance of the insurance company i.e.,
opposite party No.2 before the Commissioner.
2. The appellant herein is opposite party No.2, respondent Nos.1 and 2 herein are applicants and respondent No.3 herein is opposite party No.1 before the Commissioner.
For the sake of convenience, the parties are hereinafter referred to as they were arrayed before the Commissioner.
The facts of the case of the applicants are that the deceased was employed as labourer on tractor and trailer bearing Nos.AP 16 TW 3698 and AP 16 TW 3694, which is owned by opposite party No.1.
On, 26.10.2009, the deceased along with other labourers and driver of the tractor and trailer were travelling on the said vehicle during the course and out of their employment.

When, the tractor and trailer reached near Mariyamma statue turning at Kothagudem, the driver took a turn in rash and negligent manner, due to which, the deceased fell down from the trailer and sustained injuries.
He was shifted to Government Hospital, Thiruvuru, where the doctors declared that he was brought dead.
In this regard, a case was registered in Crime No.121 of 2009 on the file of the Chatrai Police Station.

4. It is further contended by the applicants that the deceased was aged about 18 years at the time of the accident and he was being paid an amount of Rs.4,000/- per month towards wages and batta at Rs.50/- per day by opposite party No.1.
The accident occurred during the course and out of his employment under opposite party No.1.
Opposite party No.1 was well aware of the accident and he visited both the place of the accident and the MGP,J CMA_622_2012 hospital.
The tractor and trailer involved in the accident was insured with opposite party No.2, which was valid as on the date of the accident.
In the said circumstances, the present claim petition is filed by the applicants against both the opposite parties seeking compensation of Rs.5,00,000/-.

sentences.text: 5. Opposite party No.1 did not appear before the Commissioner and he was set ex parte.
Opposite party No.2 filed its counter denying the occurrence of the accident, manner of the accident, age and wages paid to the deceased.
It is stated that there is no employee and employer relationship between the deceased and opposite party No.1.
It is also stated that the driver of the vehicle involved in the accident was not having valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident.

6. Opposite party No.2 filed additional counter stating that the extract of the driving license of the driver of the tractor and trailer shows that there was no endorsement of 'transport', whereas, the tractor and trailer are LMV-transport for commercial use.
As such, the driver of the tractor and trailer was not having valid and effective driving license to drive the said vehicle as on the date of accident.
Further, the fitness of the vehicle expired on MGP,J CMA_622_2012 23.08.2008.

Hence,
opposite party No.1 violated the terms and conditions of the insurance policy, as such, opposite party No.2 is not liable to pay compensation to the applicants indemnifying opposite party No.1.
Therefore, prayed to dismiss the claim petition against them.
7. In support of their case, the applicants got examined A.W.1 and got marked Exs.A-1 to A-8.
Opposite party No.2 got examined R.W.1 and got marked Exs.B-1 to B-3, in support of its case.
Further, Senior Assistant of RTA, Nuzvid, was examined as X.W.1 and Ex.X-1 was marked through his evidence.

8. On the basis of the above pleadings, the Commissioner framed the following issues for consideration:
"1.
Whether the deceased was a workman?
2. If yes, whether the deceased died due to the injuries sustained in the accident during the course and out of his employment under the employment of O.P.1?
3. Whether there was any violation of conditions of the insurance policy by O.P.1?
4. Who are liable to pay compensation to the dependants of the deceased?
5. What is the amount of compensation entitled by the dependents of the deceased?"
After considering the pleadings and evidence on record, the Commissioner held that the applicants have successfully proved their case.
Hence, the claim petition was partly allowed holding that both the opposite parties were jointly and severally liable and granted an amount of Rs.4,14,215/- towards compensation.
10. Heard, both sides.

sentences.text: Learned counsel for the appellant/opposite party No.2 i.e., the insurance company has contended that though, the applicants failed to prove that there is employee and employer relationship between the deceased and opposite party No.1, the Commissioner held that the deceased was employed under opposite party No.1.

It is further contended that the evidence on record shows that the driver of the vehicle was not holding a valid driving license, but the Commissioner without considering the same has held that opposite party No.2 is liable to pay compensation.
Therefore, prayed to allow the appeal and set aside the impugned order of the Commissioner.

12. Per contra, the learned counsel for respondent Nos.1 and 2/applicants has contended that the Commissioner has rightly MGP,J CMA_622_2012 considered the entire evidence available on record and has granted just and reasonable compensation, for which interference of this Court is unwarranted.
Hence, prayed to dismiss the appeal.

13. Now, the point for determination is as follows:
"Whether the applicants are entitled for compensation as granted by the Commissioner?"
Point:-
14. This Court has perused the entire documents and evidence placed on record by both the parties.
Applicant No.1, who is father of the deceased was got examined as A.W.1 and reiterated the contents of the claim petition.
In support of their case, he filed Exs.A-1 to A-8.
In the cross-examination, he accepted that he did not file any document to show that the deceased was employed under opposite party No.1.
He denied that the accident did not occur during the course and out of employment of the deceased under opposite party No.1.
He also denied that the driver of the tractor and trailer was not having valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident.
15. Opposite party No.2 got examined its Administrative Officer as R.W.1 and got marked Exs.B-1 to B-3.
He reiterated the MGP,J CMA_622_2012 contents of the counter filed by opposite party No.2.
He admitted that the tractor and trailer involved in the accident was having valid and effective insurance policy as on the date of the accident.
In the cross-examination, he denied the suggestions given by the appellants.
16. Before the Commissioner, the Senior Assistant, RTA Unit Office, Nizvid, Krishna District was examined as X.W.1 and Ex.X-1 was marked.
His evidence shows that the tractor and trailer involved in the accident was having valid permit from 05.02.2009 to 04.02.2010.
In the cross-examination by opposite party No.2, he denied that the vehicle was not having valid fitness as on the date of accident.

17. Coming to the employee and employer relationship between the deceased and opposite party No.1, it is pertinent to state that admittedly opposite party No.1 was set ex parte and the applicants have not filed any specific document to prove employment of the deceased.
However, Ex.A-1

3 FIR with complaint, Ex.A-2 copy of inquest report, Ex.A-3 postmortem examination report and Ex.A-4 copy of charge sheet clearly show that the deceased was employed under opposite party No.1 as labourer on tractor and MGP,J CMA_622_2012 trailer bearing Nos. AP 16 TW 3698 and AP 16 TW 3694.
Further, as on the date of accident, he was working in the capacity of labourer on the said tractor and trailer and in the accident, the deceased sustained injuries and succumbed to the same.
Furthermore, Ex.A-5 and Ex.A-6 copies of registration certificates of the tractor and trailer clearly reflect the name of opposite party No.1 as owner.
All these documents clearly demonstrate that the deceased was employed under opposite party No.1 as labourer and he died in the accident during the course and out of his employment.

Hence, the Commissioner has rightly considered that the applicants established employee and employer relationship between the deceased and opposite party No.1 and such findings of the Commissioner does not require any interference by this Court.
18.

Learned counsel for the appellant/opposite party No.2 contended that the driver of the tractor and trailer involved in the accident was not having valid and effective driving license as on the date of the accident.
Admittedly, the applicants have not filed any document to show that the driver of the tractor and trailer was having valid driving license.
However, opposite party No.2, through R.W.1 got marked Ex.B-2 which is extract of driving MGP,J CMA_622_2012 license of the driver of the vehicle involved in the accident.
The said document shows that the driver of the tractor and trailer was having license to drive non-transport-tractor and trailer and there was no endorsement of 'transport'.
Therefore, it is contended that he was not having valid driving license to drive the tractor and trailer involved in the accident.

19. It is pertinent to state that the claim petition of the applicants is filed under the provisions of Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923, which do not mandate that if a driver is employed, he should possess valid license as is required in terms of the mandate of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988.
However, in the case on hand, the driver was having driving license to drive the non-transport-tractor and trailer.

Moreover, the policy conditions regarding driver not holding valid and effective driving license at the time of accident cannot be considered as fundamental breach that had contributed to the cause of the accident to discharge opposite party No.2 from the liability.

Moreover, when two views are possible, the view that is beneficial to the applicants has to be taken,
since the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923, is a beneficial legislation meant to protect the interest of employees and MGP,J CMA_622_2012 workers.

Considering all these aspects, the Commissioner has rightly held that the driver of the tractor and trailer was holding valid driving license and that both the opposite parties are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the applicants.
Hence, the contention of the learned counsel for the appellant/opposite party No.2 with regard to driving license is unmerited and the same is rejected.

20. The Commissioner has considered the age of the deceased as 18 years based on the evidence available on record and he has determined the wages of the deceased at Rs.3,647.75/- considering the minimum rates of wages prevailing at that point of time.
Therefore, this Court feels that no interference is required with regard to the said aspects.

21. Coming to all other aspects, this Court is of the considered opinion that the findings of the Commissioner do not suffer from any perversity or illegality and interference of this Court is not United India Insurance Company Ltd., vs Sri B.Ananda Rao And 2 Others on 15 December, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/152587885/

In the result, the Civil Miscellaneous Appeal is dismissed by confirming the order dated 16.12.2010 in W.C.No.164 of 2009 on the file of the Commissioner for Workmen's Compensation and Assistant Commissioner of Labour-II, Hyderabad.
There shall be no order as to costs.
Miscellaneous applications pending, if any, shall stand closed.
